name: Soravex
subcategory: social lubricant — inhibition modulator and social cognition enhancer
description: Soravex is a GABA-modulator and social-cognition enhancer that reduces social anxiety, sharpens real-time social signal reading, and produces a warm, confident affect without the cognitive impairment of alcohol or the jitteriness of stimulants. It was developed as an anxiolytic alternative and is widely prescribed — but its recreational use as a social tool, networking drug, and seduction aid has overtaken its clinical applications. Novafold markets it with the slogan 'Be the person you meant to be.'
effects: elimination of social anxiety and self-consciousness
enhanced reading of social cues and body language
heightened charisma as perceived by others
side_effects: overconfidence leading to social errors that feel fine in the moment
difficulty reading authentic emotional responses vs. performance while on drug
chronic use atrophies natural social skills
dependency: users feel socially incompetent without it
can be used to lower targets' guard for manipulation or coercion
cultural_context: Soravex is so normalized in GLMZ that asking whether someone is 'Smooth' before a meeting is standard professional etiquette in Tier 3-4. Job interviews, first dates, sales calls, negotiations — it is the coffee of social pharmaceuticals. On the Shelf, it's called Charmer and is used for everything from getting past bouncers to extracting information from marks. Novafold has lobbied successfully to keep it legal by emphasizing its clinical applications, while quietly benefiting from the dependency loop it creates.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 diplomat realizes he hasn't attended a single meeting without Soravex in four years and genuinely cannot remember what his unmedicated personality is — or whether he has one
Soravex is being used systematically in Shelf community meetings by an outside NGO whose workers take it and whose local contacts don't — the power dynamic this creates is subtle but profound

A batch of counterfeit Soravex has been distributed city-wide with an unknown additive that causes users to be significantly more susceptible to suggestion — someone is running a large-scale social engineering operation
